The CCEH gives its tunes as four-part scores; this page has the melody only, read from its MIDI file and checked against its incipit, and NoteFusion's engine wrote the solfa from the notes. Questions about St. Kevin

What is the doh of St. Kevin?

In this version, in G major, doh is G. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does St. Kevin start on?

It starts on m (B in G major). Find doh first, then sing up or down to m.

What words can be sung to St. Kevin?

St. Kevin is in the metre 7.6.7.6: lines of 7, 6, 7, 6 syllables. Words written in the same metre fit it, such as Abide, O Dearest Jesus, O Lord, I Am Not Worthy; check where the stresses fall before you sing them together.

Is St. Kevin in the public domain?

Yes. Arthur Seymour Sullivan died in 1900; the tune was first published in 1872. Everyone named died before 1955 and it was published before 1929, so the tune is out of copyright in Nigeria, the UK, the EU and the United States. Modern arrangements of it can still be under copyright.
